text:
Fixed and verified.

Rejection was placed at NativeOption.from (core/SiteProfile.scala) rather than in the renderer, so a conflicting option cannot be CONSTRUCTED at all. The site allowlist could never have fixed this: it is an allowlist, so it can admit a reserved name but never reserve one, and an operator who allowlisted "output" got a silent override of the planner's log path with no diagnostic.

Reserved set derived by enumerating every option SlurmCommands actually renders: account, array, constraint, container, cpus-per-task, error, export, format, gres, job-name, jobs, json, mem, mem-per-cpu, nodes, ntasks, output, parsable, partition, qos, time. Name SYNTAX was already validated; name OWNERSHIP was not.

Why it mattered: sbatch honours the LAST occurrence of a repeated option and SlurmCommands.scala:111 appends native options after every typed one, so a native "output" replaced the log path the planner established and a native "parsable" would have broken SbatchParsable.parse outright.

Verification: 3 new tests in core/NativeOptionOwnershipSuite, including one asserting rejection is independent of the allowlist. Full suite 328, 0 failed. scalafmt clean.
